findings.summary: SubsystemDisabled policy evaluation drops the subsystem identity
findings.details: The S13-T03 contract requires independent kill switches and typed failure paths per risky subsystem. evaluateOperationPolicy destructures state/generation/expectedGeneration/expiresAt/now but ignores the supplied subsystem, and when state is disabled it returns SubsystemDisabled with subsystem set to the literal string "disabled". That means the typed error payload does not identify capture/backfill/classification/etc., weakening the contract consumers need to diagnose and stop each subsystem independently. Suggested fix: Pass the requested subsystem through evaluateOperationPolicy and construct SubsystemDisabled with that subsystem; add a focused assertion that a disabled classification/export/etc. policy returns SubsystemDisabled carrying the same subsystem value.
evidence: packages/convex/confect/ops/brainOperationPolicy.ts:125-158 constructs new SubsystemDisabled({ subsystem: "disabled" }) for any disabled policy instead of the input subsystem.

packages/convex/test/brain-operation-policy.test.ts:110-126 covers classification disabled only by matching { ok: false, errorTag: "SubsystemDisabled" }, so the incorrect subsystem payload is not caught.
Task plan S13-T03 requires independent kill switches and typed errors/state including SubsystemDisabled for subsystem-scoped operation policy.
